clue.text: Eager demon before a match not lacking heart

indicators.note: a word lacking its heart has had its central letter taken away
one thing set before another means the pieces are read in that left-to-right order

parts.note: an imp is a small demon
taken as written
a tie is a match or fixture in a cup competition
the word not with its middle letter dropped

explanation.surface: A devil itching to get on with a contest, with some complaint about its heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not lacking heart' reads like a double negative, but it simply tells you to cut the middle out of the word 'not'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone impatient is keen for things to happen at once, restless and unwilling to wait.

clue.text: Format mainly designed to be provocative

indicators.note: something designed has been laid out afresh, so these letters are put into a new pattern

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, not a signal to shorten anything

explanation.surface: A layout chosen chiefly to stir people up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mainly' looks like a cue to drop a last letter; here every letter of it is needed in the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Inflammatory words are meant to arouse anger or strong feeling, which is what provocative remarks do.

clue.text: Friend not clear about right method of fortune-telling

parts.note: a pal is a friend

indicators.note: one word placed about another wraps around it, so the short piece goes inside

parts.note: misty weather or vision is not clear
R is the usual abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A pal is vague about the proper way to tell fortunes.
explanation.definitionFit: Palmistry predicts someone's future by reading the lines on the palm of their hand.

clue.text: Strain without opening lock

indicators.note: without its opening means the first letter of the word is removed

parts.note: stress is strain or pressure

explanation.surface: Tugging at a lock that will not open.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a door lock; the definition is a lock of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A tress is a long lock of hair, a poetic word for a strand or curl.

clue.text: Tea before the usual time holding amount of work up

indicators.note: one word holding another keeps it inside itself

parts.note: early means before the expected time

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: the erg is a unit of work in physics

explanation.surface: Having tea early while holding up a workload.
explanation.walkthrough: The erg is a small physics unit of work or energy, common in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Earl Grey is a black tea blend flavoured with bergamot oil, so it is a type of tea.

clue.text: Gossip, tons and tons in story

indicators.note: these letters placed in a word are set inside it

parts.note: a tale is a story
T is the abbreviation for ton
a second ton, another T

explanation.surface: Masses of gossip in a story.
explanation.definitionFit: To tattle is to chatter idly or tell tales about others, which is gossiping.

clue.text: Front of ship supporting weight

parts.note: pro means in favour of
W is the abbreviation for weight

explanation.surface: The bow of a vessel bearing a heavy load.
explanation.definitionFit: The prow is the pointed forward part of a vessel's hull, its bow.

clue.text: Write note on amount paid for festival

parts.note: to pen is to write
te is a note of the sol-fa scale
the cost is what you pay

explanation.surface: Jotting down the price of tickets for a festival.
explanation.definitionFit: Pentecost, or Whitsun, is the Christian feast seven weeks after Easter.

clue.text: Musical drama in old age retaining power

indicators.note: something retaining a thing keeps it inside

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for old
an era is an age
P is the symbol for power

explanation.surface: A singer in old age who still keeps a powerful voice.
explanation.definitionFit: Opera is staged drama set to music, with the parts sung throughout.

clue.text: Barriers broken by real pest involved in deceptive behaviour

indicators.note: a word broken by others is split open so they sit inside it

parts.note: fences are barriers

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so these letters are mixed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written for mixing

explanation.surface: A genuine nuisance damages fences while up to some trickery.
explanation.definitionFit: Obtaining something under false pretences means doing it by lying or misrepresentation, which is deceitful conduct.

clue.text: Shrewd sellers newly disposing of large piece of furniture

indicators.note: newly suggests made over again, so the letters are rearranged
disposing of something gets rid of it, so that letter is taken away

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
L is the abbreviation for large, here removed

explanation.surface: Canny dealers clearing out a big item of furniture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Large' seems to describe the furniture, but it is the L dropped from the letters; only one L of sellers goes.
explanation.definitionFit: A Welsh dresser is a tall wooden cupboard with open shelves above for displaying plates, a substantial furniture item.

clue.text: Sign changes, losing volume

indicators.note: losing a letter means that letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: varies means changes
V is the abbreviation for volume, here removed

explanation.surface: A notice that alters as the sound is turned down.
explanation.definitionFit: Aries, the Ram, is the first of the twelve signs of the zodiac.

clue.text: Horse in endless action after record back in time of greatest achievement

indicators.note: one piece after another is placed to its right
back means the word is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: a log is a written record

indicators.note: one word in another is placed inside it
endless means the final letter is cut off

parts.note: a deed is an action
a nag is an old horse

explanation.surface: A racehorse in ceaseless action after setting a record, in its glory days.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Action' loses its last letter before the horse goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A golden age is the period when a nation, art or person flourished most.

clue.text: Items as arranged for artist

indicators.note: arranged means set out in a new order, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Objects laid out for a painter's still life.
explanation.definitionFit: Henri Matisse was a French painter, a leader of the Fauvist movement.

clue.text: Cool gains for excited Democrat

indicators.note: excited means stirred up, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written for mixing
D is the abbreviation for Democrat

explanation.surface: Calm progress for an agitated Democratic politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cool' looks like an adjective but is the noun: composure.
explanation.definitionFit: Sangfroid is composure under pressure, the noun sense of keeping one's head.

clue.text: Saint surrounded by snakes and crows

indicators.note: a thing surrounded by another sits inside it

parts.note: boas are large constricting snakes
ST is the abbreviation for saint

explanation.surface: A saint hemmed in by serpents and black birds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crows' looks like the birds but is the verb: brags.
explanation.definitionFit: To crow is to gloat or brag loudly, the same as boasting.

clue.text: Bird coming from south to north, swallow around church

indicators.note: one word around another encloses it

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for south
taken as written
N is the abbreviation for north
to swallow food is to eat it
CH is the abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: A migrating bird flying north, with a swallow circling a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'From south to north' looks like an instruction to read upwards, but it is taken literally, and swallow is a verb, not the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The stonechat is a small European songbird whose call sounds like two stones knocked together.

clue.text: Plant, cut by me, covering a bit

indicators.note: a word cut by another is split open with it set inside

parts.note: to sow seed is to plant it
taken as written
a hat is a head covering

explanation.surface: A gardener trims a plant while partly covering it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Covering a bit' reads as one phrase, but the definition is just 'a bit'.
explanation.definitionFit: Somewhat means to some extent or rather, a little, just as 'a bit' does.

clue.text: Difficult hearing

definitions.meaning: first meaning: hard to bear, wearing
second meaning: the judging of a case in court

explanation.walkthrough: 'Difficult hearing' sounds like being hard of hearing; the words are two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A trying day is an exhausting one, and the trying of a case is its trial before a court.

clue.text: Audibly dismissed, revolutionary pair left

parts.note: a batsman dismissed in cricket is out

indicators.note: revolutionary suggests turning round, so the words are read backwards

parts.note: a duo is a pair
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A rebel couple sent away, leaving noisily.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something out loud means speaking it so that others can hear.

clue.text: Hero, dedicated, partly undermined

indicators.note: partly means only part of these words is used, the run of letters across them

parts.note: the letters run from inside the first word into the second

explanation.surface: A devoted hero, only partly sabotaged.
explanation.definitionFit: Something eroded has been gradually worn away, as a cliff is undermined by the sea.

clue.text: Strengthen control, following evil creature east

parts.note: to rein in is to control
F is the abbreviation for following
an orc is a monster of fantasy fiction
E is the abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: Tightening control as an evil monster heads east.
explanation.definitionFit: To reinforce a wall or argument is to make it stronger by adding support.

clue.text: One understanding dream

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a deal is an understanding or agreement

explanation.surface: A single person with an understanding of dreams.
explanation.definitionFit: An ideal is a perfect standard one aspires to, a dream of how things should be.

clue.text: Diving bird black in colour apart from tail

indicators.note: a letter in a word is set inside it
apart from its tail means the final letter is left off

parts.note: green is a colour
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A diving bird in black plumage except for its tail.
explanation.definitionFit: Grebes are waterbirds that dive underwater to catch fish.

clue.text: Fuss raised about last item of menu after good cheese

indicators.note: placed after means it follows the other piece

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for good

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means the word reads upwards
one word about another surrounds it

parts.note: ado is fuss

indicators.note: the last item of a word is its final letter

parts.note: the final letter of menu

explanation.surface: A diner kicks up a fuss about the final dish after a good cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: Gouda is a mild yellow Dutch cheese named after the town where it was traded.

clue.text: Doubts, even if temporary initially, harboured by assistants

indicators.note: something harboured by another is sheltered inside it

parts.note: seconds are assistants, as in boxing or duelling
though means even if

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of the word before it

parts.note: the first letter of temporary

explanation.surface: Uncertainty, however short-lived, is kept quiet by the helpers.
explanation.walkthrough: A second is a boxer's or duellist's helper.
explanation.definitionFit: Having second thoughts means reconsidering and doubting a decision already made.

clue.text: Happy tips in general accepted

indicators.note: the tips of words are their first and last letters

parts.note: first and last letters of general
first and last letters of accepted

explanation.surface: A cheerful general whose advice is generally welcomed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tips' sounds like advice; here it means the ends of each word.
explanation.definitionFit: Glad and happy are synonyms for feeling pleased.

clue.text: Critic's article in German about time with performer

indicators.note: with means the next piece is joined on alongside
one word about another surrounds it

parts.note: der is the masculine German word for the
T is the abbreviation for time
an actor is a performer

explanation.surface: A reviewer's piece in a German paper about the time spent with an actor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Article' suggests a newspaper piece, but it is the grammatical article, 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: A detractor disparages or belittles someone, just as a harsh critic does.
